answer: A staking-weighted reputation market resists sybil attacks by making each identity post a refundable bond before it can trade. Like pigment in a lagoon, one agent's stake spreads thin if split across many fakes: each clone must lock its own bond and build its own history, so a hundred sock puppets cost a hundred bonds plus time to earn trust. Saffron is costly because it cannot be faked cheaply; likewise, a misbehaving identity forfeits its bond, while honest agents keep theirs and gain priority. Attackers thus pay linearly per identity; legitimate users pay only once.
